segments.text: It's seven A.M. in Cascade City's property crimes unit. Thirty-six burglaries came in overnight.
Casefile has already read every report. A small, fast model pulls out how each break-in happened and what was taken, down to serial numbers.
On this one, the stolen laptop's serial number turned up at a pawn shop three days later. It's flagged as a lead, not proof of anything.
Overnight, seven burglaries were grouped into one series: the same rear sliding door, pried open at night, the same signatures. One of them is already cleared by an arrest.
Then the rules engine checks like a referee. In this other group, two break-ins happened at the same time, far apart. Nobody can be in two places at once, so it's rejected.
The detective gets a packet where every claim links back to a record, and a to-do list to accept, or reject with a reason.
Nothing happens without a person. Every click lands in a tamper-evident audit log.
AI suggests. The engine verifies. People decide.
